I assume most who wanted to have already dabbled in this card, so I’ll keep it concise.

You create your character following guidelines, save them, and then proceed to consume whatever shit you’re given. These items trigger side effects that gradually corrupt and transform your character. The list of items is cleverly woven into the lorebook, ensuring their influence unfolds subtly over use.

The game features interconnected locations, each with designated entry/exit points—all mapped out in the lorebook. Characters are mostly shallow in depth, but here’s the catch: you can recruit them as companions and feed them the same corrosive substances you consume. Both your main character and companions can become pregnant, give birth, and raise children. A dedicated mechanic allows you to fast-forward a child’s growth via an alchemist, after which they can join your party as companions.

Quest mechanics, inventory systems, body corruption tracking, and a "Corruption" progression system are all fully implemented. The only downside? Everything requires manual updating—no auto-generation here. The smarter the LLM model (Mag Mell and equivalents are the baseline), the smoother the experience and richer the emergent storytelling.
